title: Effect of Partial Slip Model on Hydrodynamic Drag
content: The relationship between partial slip flow and drag reduction mechanism of devices such as riblets or super-hydrophobic surfaces has been widely discussed in the literature. Direct numerical simulations and theoretical analyses showed that the adoption of slip length concept mimics well the flow around bodies with riblets or super- hydrophobic surfaces installed. The numerical simulations of flow around bodies covered by riblets for engineering applications are difficult to perform due to their dimensions (microns at high Reynolds numbers). The detail of flow characteristics inside the grooves can be accurately computed only by Direct Numerical Simulations (DNS), still difficult to perform at high Reynolds numbers and complex configurations. Different models have been developed in the last decade to enable the numerical simulations of riblets or superhydrophobic surfaces by RANS or LES. These methods model the drag reduction, but the analysis of some interesting effects on complex bodies with riblets, requires their adoption. In the present paper a model based on the slip length concept is applied on hydrofoils and different wing configurations showing that these models are able to predict riblets performance and some interesting features of riblets effects.
